overview: Atlassian Corporation is an enterprise software company that develops team collaboration and productivity tools, including Jira (project and issue tracking), Confluence (knowledge base and wiki), Jira Service Management (ITSM), Loom (async video), and Rovo (AI-powered search and agents). The company serves over 350,000 customers globally, including 85% of the Fortune 500, through a cloud-first subscription model with no traditional direct sales force. Atlassian's products span three growing markets — software development, work management, and service management — with a combined addressable market of approximately $67 billion.

business_model.summary: Atlassian generates revenue almost entirely from subscriptions, split across Cloud (63%), Data Center on-premise (31%), and Marketplace/other (5%). The company pioneered a low-cost, product-led growth (PLG) model where software is sold via self-service with no traditional enterprise sales team, relying on viral adoption within organizations and a land-and-expand strategy. Cloud growth accelerated to 29% YoY in Q3 FY26, reflecting increasing enterprise commitment, AI-driven cross-sell, and ongoing Data Center-to-Cloud migration. Cloud NRR of 120%+ reflects strong customer expansion driven by seat growth, edition upgrades, and cross-sell of Collections.

revenue_streams.name: Cloud
revenue_streams.notes: Q3 FY26: $1,132M, up 29% YoY — growth accelerated from the 25-26% range seen in prior quarters. Driven by paid seat expansion in Jira, Teamwork Collection AI cross-sell, DC-to-Cloud migrations, and higher ARPU. FY26 Cloud growth outlook raised to ~26.5% YoY.

revenue_streams.name: Data Center
revenue_streams.notes: Q3 FY26: $561M, up 44% YoY — outsized due to Q3 being the largest Data Center renewal quarter and a greater-than-expected EOL revenue recognition pull-forward. Q4 FY26 DC growth guided to only ~8.5%, and FY27 expected to meaningfully decelerate as EOL pull-forward laps and migrations accelerate.

revenue_streams.name: Marketplace and other
revenue_streams.notes: Q3 FY26: $94M, up 7% YoY. Third-party app sales; lower take rate on Cloud Forge apps vs. Data Center. Forge developer revenue-share reduced to 0% on first $1M lifetime earnings effective January 2026 to incentivize platform buildout.

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise and SMB; self-serve and channel partner go-to-market, with a growing enterprise direct sales motion

key_metrics.rovo_customer_ARR_lift: Rovo customers growing ARR at ~2x the rate of non-Rovo customers
key_metrics.teamwork_collection_seats: 1,000+ customers upgraded; ~2x more AI credits per paid user and 2x more active agents vs. standalone equivalents

main_competitors: Microsoft (Azure DevOps, GitHub, Teams, Planner, Loop, Copilot)
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant leader in developer project tracking (Jira) with 65%+ market share in issue tracking; named Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader in DevOps Platforms and Collaborative Work Management (both 2025 editions); Forrester Wave Leader in Enterprise Service Management (Q4 2025). Q3 FY26 represented Atlassian's largest-ever quarter for competitive ITSM displacements.

moat_factors.factor: Switching costs and deep workflow integration
moat_factors.description: Jira and Confluence are deeply embedded in daily engineering and business workflows. Years of accumulated data, customized workflows, and integrations make migration expensive and disruptive. Data Center to Cloud migrations themselves are multi-year programs for large enterprises.

moat_factors.factor: Teamwork Graph and proprietary AI data
moat_factors.description: Atlassian's Teamwork Graph connects work, knowledge, people, and code across all products in a unified context layer powering Rovo AI. MCP usage within the Teamwork Graph is doubling month-over-month as third-party agents plug in via the MCP Gallery. This proprietary data advantage is difficult to replicate and creates a virtuous flywheel: more collections adopted means a richer graph, which improves AI output, which drives further adoption.

The Atlassian Marketplace has thousands of third-party apps. Partners build on the Forge platform, increasing stickiness. MCP Gallery expansions (Amplitude, Box, Canva, Figma, GitHub, Intercom, New Relic) extend Rovo agent capabilities across the enterprise toolchain, increasing platform lock-in.

moat_factors.factor: Brand recognition in developer and technical community
moat_factors.description: Jira and Confluence are near-universal standards in software development. Over 60% of the Forbes AI 50 companies use Atlassian's System of Work. Bottom-up adoption by developers creates organic enterprise penetration that is difficult to displace.

Historically a competitive advantage in SMB, now evolving as Atlassian builds enterprise direct sales capacity. Sales and marketing as a percent of revenue remains below traditional enterprise SaaS peers, though this gap is narrowing. James Chuong (new CFO, ex-LinkedIn) is focused on driving 'durable, profitable growth.'

The System of Work vision connects technical and business teams via Teamwork, Service, and Software Collections on a single platform. Over 60% of Service Collection instances serve non-IT functions (HR, legal, finance, marketing), expanding TAM and deepening enterprise stickiness. Collections drive 10%+ seat expansion over standalone equivalents.

weaknesses: Microsoft's scale and bundling (M365/GitHub/Azure DevOps/Copilot) can undercut pricing and leverage existing enterprise relationships
Historically weak in pure enterprise sales motion; only recently investing heavily in enterprise GTM via direct sales build-out
Data Center customers may migrate to competitors (especially ServiceNow or Microsoft) rather than Atlassian Cloud during EOL transition
Rovo AI capabilities must continue proving ROI vs. Microsoft Copilot and AI-native tools to justify premium pricing
Customer support quality issues historically; restructured support org in Q1 FY26 with continued headcount rebalancing in Q3 FY26

growth_drivers: Data Center to Cloud migration: ~350K Data Center customers being moved to cloud by 2029 EOL deadline; migrations contributing mid-to-high single-digit points to Cloud revenue growth in FY26, expected to continue multi-year

AI monetization via Rovo and Collections: Service Collection eclipsed $1B ARR (30%+ YoY growth); Teamwork Collection driving 2x AI credit usage and 2x agents vs. standalone; Rovo AI credit consumption growing 20%+ MoM; Rovo customers growing ARR at 2x the rate of non-Rovo customers — AI is now measurably correlated with seat expansion and ARR acceleration

Enterprise upmarket: Record $1M+ ACV deals, 600+ customers with $1M+ ARR; RPO of $4.0B (+37% YoY) reflects deepening multi-year enterprise commitments; Q3 FY26 was largest-ever quarter for competitive ITSM displacements

Service Management expansion beyond IT: 65K+ JSM customers including 50%+ of Fortune 500; enterprise ARR growing 50%+ YoY; over 60% of Service Collection instances now serve non-IT functions (HR, finance, legal, marketing), validating the enterprise platform vision

Agent orchestration as new paradigm: Agents in Jira now GA — teams assign work directly to Rovo and third-party MCP-enabled agents, with full audit trails and governance; Rovo Service (generally available) executes employee support and onboarding workflows autonomously; agentic automation runs growing 30% MoM with Service Collection driving 50% of total agentic runs

Geographic expansion and regulated industries: EMEA at 41% of revenue; Government Cloud (FedRAMP) and Isolated Cloud open new regulated-industry markets; Dia Reports (browser-native briefings via Teamwork Graph) adds a new entry point via The Browser Company acquisition

Team '26 conference momentum: Conference in Anaheim (May 2026) showcased agents across the platform, Jira Product Discovery Enterprise GA, and expanded Teamwork Graph openness to outside agents — reinforcing platform ecosystem depth

Restructuring-funded reinvestment: $224M Q3 restructuring (10% headcount reduction) expected to generate savings reinvested in AI and enterprise sales in FY27, improving operating leverage while maintaining growth investment

business.description: Microsoft bundles Azure DevOps, GitHub (100M+ developers), Teams, Planner, Loop, and Copilot into M365/Azure agreements. Enterprise CFOs consolidating vendors may displace Atlassian, particularly for smaller customers where Atlassian's breadth advantage is less compelling. Microsoft's Copilot is now embedded across the same workflows where Rovo competes.

AI-native project management and coding tools (Linear, GitHub issues + Copilot, Cursor, etc.) could reduce reliance on Jira for software teams. Management cites data showing AI developer tool users expand Jira seats faster, but this dynamic may not persist if AI further automates task creation and reduces the need for structured workflow tools.

Large enterprise customers (especially regulated industries) face complex, multi-year migrations. Risk of customer churn to competitors during migration window, particularly from ServiceNow or Microsoft offering migration incentives. The 2029 EOL deadline creates urgency but also opens a competitive window. Atlassian Ascend program mitigates but does not eliminate this risk.

No single customer represents a material percentage of revenue, but a high volume of SMB/mid-market customers means economic downturns can pressure net seat expansion rates. Management acknowledges macro and geopolitical uncertainty in guidance framing.

Atlassian spent approximately $1.6B in FY26 H1 on DX and The Browser Company. Integrating products and cultures while maintaining execution on core business is a risk. Dia Reports (launched at Team '26) is an early integration product from The Browser Company, but enterprise browser adoption remains unproven at scale.

financial.risk: Data Center revenue cliff in FY27
financial.description: Management explicitly warned that Data Center revenue growth will meaningfully decelerate in FY27 as the FY26 EOL revenue recognition pull-forward benefit (worth approximately 11.5+ percentage points of DC growth in FY26) unwinds. Q3 FY26 saw 44% DC growth partly due to pull-forward of customer purchasing; Q4 FY26 is guided to only 8.5% DC growth. In FY27, DC revenue could decline in absolute terms if migrations accelerate. Total company revenue growth rate may decelerate even if the business is fundamentally healthy.

financial.risk: GAAP profitability and high stock-based compensation
financial.description: Atlassian remains GAAP operating-loss negative. Q3 FY26 GAAP operating margin was (3%), including $224M restructuring charges. Full-year FY26 GAAP operating margin guided to (2.0%). SBC remains ~23-25% of revenue on a non-GAAP-adjusted basis. The restructuring is designed to accelerate the path to GAAP profitability; Q4 FY26 is guided to 4.5% GAAP operating margin. Diluted share count now expected to decrease approximately 2.5% in FY26 (improved from prior guidance of less than 1% growth), reflecting $991M of buybacks in Q3 alone.
With 52% of revenue from outside the Americas, USD strength creates headwinds to reported revenue. Atlassian uses FX hedges but currency remains a material variable.

Growing Rovo AI credit consumption (20%+ MoM growth) creates increasing AI compute costs. Management expects continued Cloud infrastructure optimization to offset cost pressure at current scale, but as agentic usage and Rovo deployment accelerates, compute costs could pressure non-GAAP gross margins. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 89% in Q3 FY26, above prior guidance, suggesting optimization is currently working.

regulatory.description: Enterprise and government customers increasingly require data residency in specific jurisdictions. Atlassian is expanding data residency options and building Isolated Cloud and Government Cloud, but falling behind competitors on these requirements could delay enterprise migrations.

Evolving AI regulations (EU AI Act, US executive orders) could impose compliance costs or restrict certain AI capabilities embedded in Atlassian products. Atlassian's agent governance features (audit trails, admin controls, human supervision) appear designed in part to address regulatory requirements proactively.

macro.description: Enterprise software spending is correlated with developer headcount and overall IT budgets. A recession or significant tech-sector layoffs would directly impact seat counts and expansion rates. Management takes a 'thoughtful and prudent approach' to guidance that incorporates macro and geopolitical uncertainty.

A scenario where AI dramatically reduces the number of software engineers, rather than augmenting them, could structurally reduce demand for developer tooling. Atlassian is partially hedging this by expanding into business-team workflows (50%+ of core product users are now from non-technical teams) and building AI agents as the new unit of work.

execution.risk: Enterprise GTM maturation and restructuring integration
execution.description: Atlassian conducted a 10% headcount reduction (~1,600 employees) in Q3 FY26, with over 900 roles cut in R&D. New CFO James Chuong (former LinkedIn CFO, joined March 30, 2026) brings enterprise finance discipline but is new to the company. Prior President Anu Bharadwaj departed December 2025. Managing a major restructuring while simultaneously scaling an enterprise direct sales motion elevates execution risk.

The $610M acquisition of The Browser Company to build an enterprise AI browser is a high-risk strategic bet. Dia Reports (browser-native briefings via Teamwork Graph) was launched at Team '26 as an early product, but enterprise browser adoption (vs. Chrome/Edge) remains a long road. Path to ROI is unclear within a 3-5 year investment horizon.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Enterprise collaboration software market growing 13% annually; software development tooling growing 9% annually; IT/enterprise service management growing 13% annually. AI is accelerating platform consolidation as enterprises seek unified systems of work over point solutions. Atlassian's $67B SAM is growing across three markets with significant penetration runway, especially in service management and non-technical business workflows. Gartner estimates 30% of organizations will achieve autonomous digital workplace operations for 80% of services by 2030 (up from 0% in 2025), a dynamic that directly favors Atlassian's agentic ITSM strategy.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - primarily a recurring subscription business anchored to developer headcount and enterprise IT budgets. Resilient in mild recessions due to mission-critical workflow embedding, but vulnerable to significant developer layoffs or IT spending freezes. Atlassian's own Q3 FY26 restructuring (10% headcount cut) is notable in the context of broader industry cost discipline.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct impact. Atlassian has minimal debt ($989M long-term, fixed-rate senior notes due 2029/2034). Indirect impact via tech valuation multiples — as a high-multiple growth stock, TEAM has been sensitive to risk-free rate changes. At ~$79/share as of June 30, 2026, the stock has declined significantly from prior peaks amid broader software multiple compression.
key_input_costs: AI model compute (Anthropic/Google Gemini/OpenAI APIs — Atlassian added Gemini 3 Flash in Q3)
Real estate (consolidating footprint via Q3 restructuring lease consolidations)
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Significant - 52% of revenue from outside Americas. Primary exposures in EUR, GBP, AUD. Uses FX forward contracts for hedging.
macro_factors.regulatory_environment: Benign currently. Atlassian operates in the enterprise SaaS space without meaningful antitrust exposure. Data privacy (GDPR, CCPA) compliance is a standard cost of doing business. Government Cloud launch opens FedRAMP-regulated markets. EU AI Act compliance costs are a watch item.

recent_developments.event: Q3 FY26 results (quarter ended March 31, 2026): Total revenue $1,787M, up 32% YoY, beating guidance of $1,689-1,697M by approximately $90M. Cloud revenue $1,132M, up 29% YoY (accelerating from 26% in Q2 FY26 and 25% in Q3 FY25). Non-GAAP operating margin 34%, up 8 percentage points YoY. Free cash flow $561M, FCF margin 31%. Raised FY26 guidance: total revenue growth to approximately 24% YoY; Cloud growth to 26.5% YoY; non-GAAP operating margin to 29.0% for FY26.

Service Collection eclipsed $1 billion in ARR, growing over 30% YoY. Q3 FY26 was Atlassian's largest-ever quarter for competitive ITSM displacements. Enterprise ARR within Service Collection growing 50%+ YoY. Over 60% of Service Collection instances now serve non-IT functions (HR, legal, finance, marketing).

Rovo AI monetization traction confirmed: Rovo customers growing ARR at ~2x the rate of non-Rovo customers. AI credit usage growing 20%+ month-over-month. Teamwork Collection customers use approximately 2x more AI credits per paid user and have 2x more active agents vs. standalone equivalents. Agentic automation runs growing 30% MoM, with Service Collection driving 50% of total agentic runs across the platform.

James Chuong officially became CFO (formerly CFO of LinkedIn for 13 years, overseeing growth to 1B members and $18B revenue). Appointment announced February 18, 2026 and effective March 30, 2026, completing the CFO transition from retiring Joe Binz. Chuong's first public appearance as CFO was the Q3 FY26 earnings call.

Atlassian announced a workforce restructuring, reducing headcount by approximately 10% (~1,600 employees). Over 900 roles were in R&D. Total restructuring charges of $224M recognized in Q3 FY26, comprising $170M severance/termination benefits and $54M lease consolidation. Strategic rationale: self-fund AI and enterprise sales investment, reorganize around the System of Work, and accelerate path to GAAP profitability.

Team '26 conference in Anaheim (May 5-7, 2026): Key announcements included Agents in Jira reaching general availability, Jira Product Discovery Enterprise GA, Dia Reports (proactive browser-native briefings via Teamwork Graph from The Browser Company acquisition), expanded MCP Gallery for Rovo agent integrations, and Teamwork Graph opened to external agents via new CLI and MCP server. CEO and co-founder Mike Cannon-Brookes framed Atlassian's pitch as the infrastructure for the 'AI-native organization.'

Post-Q3 analyst reactions: Mixed sentiment despite strong beat. Stock rose approximately 30% immediately post-earnings. Barclays raised price target to $106 (Overweight). Cantor Fitzgerald cut to $98 (Overweight). Oppenheimer cut to $100 (Outperform). BofA cut to $84 (Buy). Average Street target approximately $130. Broader software multiple compression cycle weighed on valuations despite operational outperformance.
Completed acquisition of DX (engineering intelligence/developer productivity platform) for approximately $1 billion. DX contributing approximately 1 percentage point to FY26 Cloud revenue growth.
Tamar Yehoshua joined as Chief Product and AI Officer, formerly President of Product and Technology at Glean and CPO at Slack. Leads product and AI strategy.
Completed acquisition of The Browser Company of New York (Arc and Dia AI browsers) for approximately $610M. First product integration — Dia Reports — launched at Team '26 in May 2026.

Announced end-of-life for Data Center products by March 28, 2029. Launched Atlassian Ascend migration program. Introduced Data Center EOL revenue recognition change, where a higher proportion of DC subscription contract value is recognized upfront as term license revenue, providing a near-term revenue tailwind that is expected to reverse meaningfully in FY27.

items.vs_prior: to be updated at FY26 close
items.notes: Prior FY27 non-GAAP operating margin target of 25%+ was set before the restructuring. Given Q3 FY26 non-GAAP operating margin of 34% and restructuring-driven savings being partly reinvested in AI and enterprise sales in FY27, full FY27 guidance will be provided with Q4 FY26 results.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes: 'Service Collection scaled past $1B+ in ARR, growing over 30% year-over-year, as it continues to take share and reinforce our conviction in the long-term growth opportunity of the Atlassian System of Work.' On AI: 'Customers using Rovo are growing their ARR at 2x the rate of those who aren't — they're voting with their wallets.' New CFO James Chuong: 'Cloud revenue growth accelerated to 29% year-over-year as customers deepen their engagement with our System of Work... I'm excited about the significant opportunity ahead to drive durable, profitable growth as we scale.' Management consistently flagged macro and geopolitical uncertainty as a risk factor informing their prudent guidance approach.

bull_case: Cloud growth is accelerating, not decelerating: Q3 FY26 Cloud revenue grew 29% YoY, up from 25-26% in prior quarters. The combination of DC-to-Cloud migrations, Teamwork/Service Collection cross-sell, and AI-driven seat expansion provides multiple concurrent levers. With FY26 Cloud growth now guided at 26.5% and the DC migration pipeline multi-year, Cloud can sustain 25%+ growth through FY28.

AI monetization is now measurably correlated with revenue acceleration: Rovo customers are growing ARR at 2x the rate of non-Rovo customers — a key proof point that AI is pulling revenue forward, not just being a feature. AI credit consumption growing 20%+ MoM and agentic runs growing 30% MoM signal that customers are deploying agents at scale. Service Collection's $1B ARR milestone with 30%+ growth, driven partly by AI capabilities, validates the AI-native service management thesis.

Restructuring creates a structurally more profitable business: The Q3 FY26 restructuring (10% headcount, $224M charges) generated employment expense savings that drove non-GAAP operating margin to 34% in Q3 — 8 ppts above the prior year and well above the 27.5% guided figure. Management plans to reinvest a portion of savings in AI and enterprise sales in FY27, but the underlying cost discipline should drive a structurally higher margin profile and accelerates the path to GAAP profitability (Q4 FY26 guided at 4.5% GAAP operating margin).

Enterprise momentum is durable and visible: RPO of $4.0B (+37% YoY) provides multi-year revenue visibility. 600+ customers with $1M+ ARR, enterprise ARR in Service Collection growing 50%+ YoY, and Q3 FY26 being the largest-ever quarter for competitive ITSM displacements all confirm the enterprise transition is real. Atlassian is taking share from ServiceNow with a more modern, AI-native, lower-cost platform.

Significant capital return to shareholders: $991M of buybacks in Q3 FY26 alone (4% of shares), with $2.2B of authorization remaining. Diluted share count expected to shrink approximately 2.5% in FY26. Founders previously paused their own selling programs. Combined with $1.4B+ annual FCF generation, Atlassian has capacity for continued aggressive buybacks that create per-share value even if revenue growth moderates.
bear_case: Data Center revenue cliff makes FY27 guidance a major overhang: Management has explicitly warned of 'meaningful deceleration' in FY27 Data Center revenue. The Q3 FY26 DC growth of 44% was artificially inflated by pull-forward of customer purchasing and EOL recognition; Q4 FY26 is already guided to 8.5%. In FY27, DC revenue could decline in absolute terms if migrations run ahead of schedule. Total company revenue growth may decelerate to the mid-teens or below in FY27, creating a perception problem and multiple compression risk.

Microsoft's bundling threat is intensifying: Microsoft has GitHub (100M+ developers), Azure DevOps, Teams, Planner, Copilot (embedded AI), and M365 — all increasingly integrated. Microsoft can bundle these tools at discounts that Atlassian cannot match, particularly as enterprise CFOs under cost pressure seek vendor consolidation. Atlassian has no clear defense if Microsoft decides to aggressively discount developers into Azure DevOps ecosystems. The post-Q3 analyst target cuts (BofA to $84, Oppenheimer to $100, Cantor Fitzgerald to $98) partly reflect this competitive concern.

Software multiple compression is punishing the stock despite strong execution: TEAM has declined significantly from peak levels, with the stock at approximately $79 as of June 30, 2026, despite Q3 results that beat guidance by approximately $90M on revenue and delivered 34% non-GAAP operating margin. The broader enterprise software re-rating cycle is compressing multiples for all growth stocks. Atlassian's valuation remains elevated relative to its own history, meaning any execution stumble could trigger further de-rating.

GTM transition and leadership change risk remains elevated: The enterprise direct sales build-out is the most complex go-to-market transition in Atlassian's history, being managed simultaneously with a major restructuring (10% headcount cut, 900+ R&D roles eliminated) and a new CFO (James Chuong, in seat since March 30, 2026) who is still in the learning phase. President Anu Bharadwaj departed December 2025. Multiple leadership transitions during a critical strategic inflection point elevate execution risk.

AI monetization is still nascent relative to investment: Despite 20%+ MoM AI credit growth, AI has not yet generated a distinct, separately disclosed revenue contribution that the market can size. The Browser Company/Dia AI browser bet ($610M) produced Dia Reports at Team '26 but enterprise browser adoption against Chrome and Edge is a long and uncertain journey. If AI monetization disappoints relative to the R&D and compute investment required, or if the restructuring savings are fully absorbed by AI investment without margin expansion, the FY27 profitability narrative could underperform expectations.
